Saudi Arabia End of Service Calculator

Enter your last monthly wage, your start date and last working day, and why your contract ended. The award appears instantly, with the article of law behind each figure.

Prepared and reviewed by the Mustahaqati team · Last updated: 2026-11-03

Calculate your end-of-service award

Basic salary plus fixed allowances (housing, transport…): the "actual wage" in the law.

How the Saudi end-of-service award is calculated

ServiceFull award (Article 84)On resignation (Article 85)
Less than 2 yearsHalf a month per yearNothing
2 to 5 yearsHalf a month per yearOne third
More than 5, under 10 yearsHalf a month for each of the first 5, then a full monthTwo thirds
10 years or moreHalf a month for each of the first 5, then a full monthFull award

Example: last wage SAR 9,000 and 8 years of service. First five years: 5 × 4,500 = 22,500. Three more years: 3 × 9,000 = 27,000. Full award: SAR 49,500. On resignation (more than five years): two thirds = SAR 33,000.

Frequently asked questions

How is end of service calculated in Saudi Arabia?

Half a month's wage for each of the first five years of service and a full month's wage for each year after that, based on the last actual wage (basic salary plus fixed allowances such as housing and transport). Part years count pro rata (Article 84).

How much do I get if I resign?

Nothing before two years of service, one third of the award from two to five years, two thirds from more than five to under ten years, and the full award after ten years (Article 85).

Do the resignation fractions apply to open-ended contracts after the 2025 amendments?

Since 19 February 2025 the law treats resignation as a fixed-term contract matter, and an employee on an open-ended contract ends it by notice under Article 75. Several practitioners argue such an employee is owed the full award, but there is no published ministry position or court principle yet, so the calculator shows the cautious figure and the full amount.

When is the full award paid despite resignation?

When a female employee resigns within six months of marriage or three months of childbirth, when the employee leaves due to force majeure (Article 87), or leaves under one of the Article 81 cases such as the employer's breach of contract.

When is no award due?

When the employer terminates the contract for one of the Article 80 cases, after giving the employee a chance to object, or when the contract ends during probation.

Sources

  • Saudi Labor Law — Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (Articles 80, 84, 85, 87; Arabic)
  • Official end-of-service calculator — Ministry of Human Resources (Arabic)
